lens_summary: Lens: ensembles, inference budget, private set. (1) There is NO spare inference budget to buy more seeds/views: our exp48/exp51-class submissions take ~7.5 h from submit to score (CONTEXT.md l.1488-1497; wf_ideas_v2 finals notes: #28 03:45->11:20), exp51 used 1,713 s on the 4 dummy clips (CONTEXT.md l.1424), and x138 has a hard-coded runtime guard: 27,000 s (7.5 h) after kernel start the repair loop switches off relink(+readmit), gap close, gap2, safe divisions and linefit for every remaining dataset (experiments/ext_x138/biohub-x138.ipynb cell 0 l.73, cell 5 l.10-45, l.2071-2116). Datasets are repaired in sorted-name order, so if the hidden run passes 7.5 h the LAST datasets (plausibly a whole embryo prefix, possibly private) lose the tail, which is worth ~0.025 per movie on the exp29 tail (RESULTS.md per-stage table: gap +0.013, divisions +0.0084, veto -0.0035, linefit +0.0145, relink -0.0067). One hidden run produces both public and private scores, so this can hit private while leaving public intact. That makes the guard the lens's biggest item: 0 on public in expectation, but a -0.005..-0.024 private loss avoided when it fires (scratchpad calc, see notes). exp57b (x138 + DaughterNet insertion) adds repair seconds outside the guard, so it reaches the 7.5 h line sooner than exp56. (2) Private transfer: the GT-vs-detection offset depends on the embryo (z bias with no head: 44b6 +0.18 um, 6bba +0.82 um; public head leaves +0.13 / +0.45; experiments/coordhead_retrain/out_full_P/report.txt). x138's node drop sits mostly on one dense 44b6 clip (-10.7%, DIFF.md s.4). And 41+ teams submit x138 byte-for-byte, so on private they will all move together. A structurally different F2 therefore pays: at mu=-0.002 the premium is +0.0008 for s=0.004 and +0.0015 for s=0.006, against +0.0002 for a near-copy (s=0.002). (3) Ensembles: TTA variants of the same model are closed (Z-flip/axis-flip ties). Blend weights are LB-sensitive (secondary weight 0.5 = 0.943 vs 0.945, CONTEXT.md l.356). Our own retrained detectors are worse (0.920 as secondary; fine-tunes 0.944/0.943). The only step-change-sized ensemble move left is a THIRD independently trained detector at a small blend weight. It has no honest local validation and costs GPU time, P(>= +0.002) ~0.2. (4) Fusing two tails on the shared ILP graph (x138 tail vs our tail; the pre-ILP output is identical, DIFF.md s.4) is capped by the 0.003 public gap between them. HONEST CEILING OF THE LENS: about +0.000..+0.004 public (expected ~+0.001) and +0.001..+0.004 expected private (insurance plus finals premium), with up to +0.01..+0.02 private protected in the bad case where the guard fires. Nothing in this lens reaches 0.99, or even 0.97. 0.99 would need adjusted edge ~0.96 plus division J ~0.3 on unseen embryos, beyond the current LB top (0.975). Of all four ideas, the budget-aware guard has the most expected value per slot.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: The x138 stack scores the same on private as on public, so an x138-based F1 is safe (the probe rule '#34 = 0.953 -> x138 is the new base').
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: x138 degrades its whole repair tail for every dataset processed after 27,000 s of kernel time. The repair loop runs in sorted-name order. One hidden run scores public and private together, so a firing guard can hit only private (or only public) datasets. 41 identical public 0.953 scores prove nothing about the datasets later in the order. Our comparable stack takes ~7.5 h from submit to score, right at the guard line. exp57b adds DaughterNet time inside the loop that the guard does not cover.

hypotheses.title: Replace x138's fixed 7.5 h repair deadline with a budget-aware one (private-set insurance for an x138-based F1)
hypotheses.mechanism: In x138 (and exp56/exp57b), every dataset whose repair starts more than 27,000 s after kernel start is written with relink (and readmit, nested inside it), gap close, gap2, safe divisions and linefit OFF. The repair loop visits datasets in sorted-name order, and one hidden run produces both public and private scores. Our comparable stack takes ~7.5 h from submit to score, so an x138 run of 7.5-8.5 h is plausible (guess). In that case the last 20-67% of datasets lose ~0.025 each (per-stage table on the exp29 tail). If those datasets are private, public shows nothing. exp57b adds DaughterNet seconds inside the loop that the guard does not cover, so it crosses the line sooner. The fix keeps the full tail as long as the real 12 h limit allows.
hypotheses.change: New patch in tools/build_probe_kernel.py for --base x138, e.g. --patch deadline (knob BIOHUB_REPAIR_BUDGET_S, default 0 = no-op). In the repair loop (x138 cell 5 near l.2115), replace `_dataset_t0 - KERNEL_START_TS > REPAIR_DEADLINE_S` with a budget test: remaining = datasets not yet repaired; est = max(60 s, 1.3 x p90 of repair_seconds so far); degrade only if elapsed + remaining x est > BUDGET (39,600 s = 11 h). Keep a hard fallback at 41,400 s (11.5 h). Log the decision per dataset. Leave ILP_TIMEOUT 1200 s unchanged: it bounds the GPU phase. Apply to whichever x138-family file becomes F1 (exp56 or exp57b), and to F2 if that is x138-based.

T=8.5 -> -0.014..-0.024 (scratchpad calc in notes). If T <= 7.5 h the gain is exactly 0 and the output is byte-identical.

The fix is weakly dominant: with no firing the file is byte-identical.
hypotheses.validation_protocol: No lab needed; the gain cannot be in-sample because it changes no model or threshold. Pre-registered steps: (1) Dummy run: CSV sha256 must equal exp56's (exp57b's for the insertion variant). (2) A second dummy run with BIOHUB_REPAIR_BUDGET_S=1 must show 'DEADLINE' on the first dataset and a valid CSV, which proves the degrade path. hypotheses.title: Choose F1/F2 for private in the x138 era: guard-safe x138-family F1 plus our-tail exp52 as a structurally different F2
hypotheses.mechanism: Kaggle scores a team by the better private score of its two finals. The expected premium of F2 over F1 is E[D+] = mu*Phi(mu/s) + s*phi(mu/s), where D is F2's private score minus F1's. Near-copies (exp56 vs exp57b differ by 12 forks; x138 vs x138+riders) have s ~0.001-0.002 and a premium <= 0.0002. exp52 (0.950: our relink, no readmit/gapfill, DivNet veto, leaf prune, DaughterNet, head, float coords) shares only the pre-ILP stage with x138, so s is larger. Evidence that private and public may differ for these stacks: the head's value depends on the embryo's annotation offset (44b6 +0.18 vs 6bba +0.82 um in z); x138's node drop is concentrated on one dense 44b6 clip; the head gave +0.007 on x138's base but +0.002 on ours. Also, 41+ teams hold x138 byte-for-byte, so an x138 private collapse (e.g. the guard) moves all of them together and F2 is the only escape. Rank value is therefore larger than the score premium.
hypotheses.change: Pre-register now, before more scores arrive. F1 = the best x138-family file (exp57b if #35 > #34, else exp56), preferably its guard-safe rebuild (idea x138-budget-aware-deadline). F2 = exp52 (already scored 0.950) if public(exp52) >= public(F1) - 0.004. Otherwise F2 = the scored x138-family file with the most different tail. Never pick F2 as the higher of two near-copies (winner's curse). No slot needed. Do not tune F2 on public (for example, no exp52 + DeepCenter 0.25 rebuild). Keep it as an already scored file.

hypotheses.title: Add a third, independently trained detector to x138's detection blend (model-diversity ensemble), paid for by the budget-aware guard
hypotheses.mechanism: x138's detections come from a heatmap blend: 0.2 x primary (support pack 50ep) + 0.8 x secondary (seed314159), each with 8-view TTA, plus a retention guard. Both are pilkwang models. Averaging an independently trained third detector lowers peak-position variance and cuts spurious single-model peaks. That is what the dual-seed blend did (mige551: -1.7% nodes and better precision; the dual-seed blend is part of the heuristics worth +0.046 on unseen embryos). It targets the lab's two biggest FN classes: ~31% of FN involve a node never detected, and ~2,700 swap FN are node-position errors (oracle +0.03-0.046). Top teams report their gains came from the detector. This is the only step-change-sized lever under the ensemble lens.
hypotheses.change: In the predict-script patch cell (x138 cell 4), load a third TemporalUNet3D-compatible checkpoint. First candidate: leonixis/biohub-v5-candidates (all 199 videos, 60 ep; alone 0.947 on Harmonic Fusion); fallback: friend A's all-199 scratch primary. Blend det = 0.2 P + (0.8 - w) S + w T with w = 0.2, using 4-view TTA for T to limit cost. The retention guard also covers T. Head, edge features and edge scorer stay on the primary's features. Must ship with the budget-aware guard (idea 1), since it adds ~15-30% of GPU time (guess).

hypotheses.title: Fuse the x138 tail and our tail on the shared ILP graph (edge consensus, geometry tie-break)
hypotheses.mechanism: exp51 and x138 have identical pre-ILP coordinates and raw ILP graphs (121,777 nodes / 114,927 edges on the dummies). They differ only in the post-ILP tail: flow-prior relink + readmit + gapfill + DeepCenter 0.25 for x138; plain relink + DivNet veto + leaf prune + DaughterNet for ours. Where the two tails give a target node the same parent, the edge is robust. Where they disagree, one tail is wrong. A per-node vote with a third, cheap voter (x138 tail with flow prior off) plus a geometry tie-break (multi-frame motion residual) could keep the better choice per node. That is edge voting across stacks without a second GPU pass.
hypotheses.change: In one x138 kernel, run both tails on each dataset's ILP graph: x138's tail and ours, ported from exp48's cell 8 as a function. Take x138's graph and, for target nodes whose parent differs, use the majority of three tails. Ties go to the smaller 3-frame motion residual. Nodes are never added or removed (so node count equals x138's), and forks are kept from x138 (+DaughterNet if #35 wins).
